title: Scheduled Fourier estimator cost
statement: Let $n$ be a nonnegative integer, let $f$ be a Boolean function on the sign cube $\\{-1,1\\}^n$, let $S\subseteq\{1,\ldots,n\}$, and let $\varepsilon,\delta\in\mathbb Q$ satisfy $0<\varepsilon,\delta\le 1/2$. Every outcome in the support of the scheduled Fourier coefficient estimator, when run on $f$, has cost $(m,0,m+m(|S|+1))$, where $m=\lceil 2b(\delta)/\varepsilon^2\rceil$ and $b(\delta)=\lceil\log_2\lceil 2/\delta\rceil\rceil$ is the specified failure-bit count.
hypotheses_covered: $f$ is a Boolean function on the sign cube
$S$ is a subset of the coordinates
the outcome belongs to the support of the estimator's cost distribution
